memory_update.text: AMAT, LRCX and KLAC are core US-listed equipment/process-control leaders for leading-edge foundry capacity expansion; they should remain in the node universe even if near-term AI scarcity centers on HBM and packaging.

ONTO and VECO are less-obvious US-listed equipment beneficiaries with direct exposure to advanced-node metrology, HBM, EUV-adjacent processes and advanced packaging; both merit follow-up evidence checks on revenue mix and customer concentration.

Test and probe-card names such as TER and FORM were not included in the five-candidate cap but should be expanded in a separate adjacent chokepoint pass focused on known-good-die, wafer probe, system-level test, HBM test and chiplet/CoW validation.

For this node, the highest-value falsification data are tool lead times, customer capex pull-ins or cancellations, cleanroom constraints, tool-of-record wins, export-control impact, advanced-packaging order durability, and foundry/logic versus memory utilization.

node: Leading-edge foundry capacity and semiconductor equipment
summary: Expanded US-listed universe for the AI leading-edge foundry and semiconductor-equipment node. The strongest direct mappings are process equipment, etch/deposition, process control, advanced-node metrology, EUV-adjacent tooling, and advanced-packaging process tools. Near-term AI scarcity may still be more acute in HBM and packaging, but these companies are slower-moving capacity enablers whose order cadence, tool-of-record status, and customer forecasts can indicate whether AI silicon supply can expand.
